steps.body: Manure: organic, rich in humus, slow nutrient release, improves soil structure, cheap, nutrients not specific. Fertiliser: inorganic, nutrient-specific (N, P, K), fast acting, does not add humus, can pollute water if overused.

steps.title: Solved: identify
steps.body: Earthworms used → vermicompost. Sun hemp ploughed in → green manure. Urea → nitrogen fertiliser.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Calling iron a macronutrient.
- Saying fertilisers improve soil structure (they don't add organic matter).
- Forgetting C, H, O come from air and water.

activity.prompt: Macronutrient or micronutrient?

quiz.q: Number of nutrients essential for plants
quiz.why: Plants need 16 nutrients for growth. Of these, 13 come from the soil and the rest from air and water.
Carbon and oxygen come from the air, and hydrogen from water. The other 13 come from the soil.
Vermicompost is made by earthworms feeding on and breaking down plant and animal waste. It enriches the soil.
Sun hemp is grown and ploughed back into the soil as green manure. It adds nutrients and organic matter.
Excess fertilisers run off into water bodies and pollute them. They don't improve soil structure or humus.
Manganese is a micronutrient, needed in small amounts. Nitrogen, potassium and magnesium are needed in large amounts.

scenes.text: The monsoon fails in Ramesh's district in August.
Farmers with wells and a village check-dam save their crop; others lose it. Irrigation and smart cropping reduce risk.

steps.title: Irrigation
steps.body:
Most Indian agriculture depends on timely monsoon rain. Irrigation systems:
- **Wells**: dug wells (shallow water-bearing strata) and tube wells (deeper strata), with pumps.
- **Canals**: water from reservoirs or rivers via main canal, branch canals and distributaries.
- **River lift systems**: water drawn directly from rivers where canal flow is insufficient.
- **Tanks**: small storage reservoirs for run-off.
Also **rainwater harvesting** and **watershed management** — small check-dams that increase groundwater and reduce run-off.

steps.title: Cropping patterns
steps.body:
- **Mixed cropping**: two or more crops grown **simultaneously on the same field** (wheat + gram, wheat + mustard, groundnut + sunflower) — reduces risk of total crop failure.
- **Inter-cropping**: two or more crops on the same field **in a definite row pattern** (e.g. one row of crop A, two rows of crop B), with different nutrient needs, e.g. soybean + maize, pearl millet (bajra) + cowpea (lobia). Pesticide application and harvesting are easier, and nutrients are used well.
- **Crop rotation**: growing different crops on a piece of land in a **pre-planned succession** (e.g. a legume after a cereal restores nitrogen). Two or three crops can be grown per year depending on duration and water.

steps.title: Solved: which pattern?
steps.body: Rows of maize alternating with rows of soybean → inter-cropping. Wheat and mustard seeds mixed and sown together → mixed cropping. Rice in kharif, then gram in rabi on the same field → crop rotation.

steps.title: Solved: why grow a legume in rotation?
steps.body: Legumes (gram, pea, pulses) host nitrogen-fixing bacteria in their root nodules, which replenish soil nitrogen used by cereals.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Confusing mixed cropping (no row pattern) with inter-cropping (definite rows).
- Saying crop rotation means rotating plants physically.

activity.prompt: Match the term with its description
pairs: Two crops sown together, no fixed rows
Two crops in a definite row pattern

quiz.q: Wheat + gram sown together on the same field
quiz.why: Growing two or more crops such as wheat and gram together on the same field is mixed cropping. In inter-cropping, they are in definite row patterns.
Soybean and maize grown in alternate rows is inter-cropping, as the pattern is fixed. Mixed cropping has no set pattern.

options: reduces risk of total crop failure
quiz.why: With mixed cropping, if one crop fails, the other may survive. This reduces the risk of total crop failure.
Small check-dams hold back water and let it soak into the ground, which is part of watershed management. They increase groundwater.

quiz.q: A legume in crop rotation helps by
quiz.why: Legumes have bacteria in their roots that fix nitrogen, so growing them in rotation adds nitrogen to the soil.

lessons.title: Crop protection and storage of grains

scenes.text: A cooperative stores 50 tonnes of wheat; months later, some sacks are damp, mouldy and chewed by rats.
Cleaning, drying, fumigation and good stores could have saved the grain.

steps.title: Weeds, pests and diseases
steps.body:
- **Weeds**: unwanted plants that compete for food, space and light, e.g. *Xanthium* (gokhroo), *Parthenium* (gajar ghas), *Cyperus rotundus* (motha). Removed mechanically, by preventive methods (proper seed-bed, timely sowing, inter-cropping, crop rotation) or with weedicides.
- **Insect pests** attack by (i) cutting roots, stems and leaves, (ii) sucking cell sap, (iii) boring into stems and fruits.
- **Diseases** are caused by bacteria, fungi and viruses — spread through soil, water and air.
Control: **pesticides** (herbicides, insecticides, fungicides) used carefully; preventive methods like resistant varieties and summer ploughing (deep ploughing to destroy weeds and pests).

steps.title: Storage of grains
steps.body:
Losses are caused by **biotic** factors (insects, rodents, fungi, mites, bacteria) and **abiotic** factors (inappropriate moisture and temperature). They cause degradation in quality, loss in weight, poor germination, discolouration and poor marketability.
Preventive and control measures: strict **cleaning** of produce, proper **drying** (first in sunlight, then in shade), and **fumigation** with chemicals that kill pests. Warehouses (godowns) are kept clean and dry.

steps.title: Solved: identify the problem
steps.body: Holes in brinjal fruit → borer pests. Grain sacks warm and damp with fungus → abiotic factors (moisture, temperature) leading to fungal attack. Parthenium spreading in a field → weed competition.

steps.title: Solved: a storage plan
steps.body: 1) Clean and dry the grain to low moisture. 2) Store in clean, dry, rodent-proof godowns on raised platforms. 3) Fumigate if pests appear. 4) Inspect regularly.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Over-using pesticides (harms health and environment).
- Storing grain while still damp.

activity.prompt: Order the steps to store harvested grain safely
items: Dry it in sunlight, then shade
Store in a clean, dry, rodent-proof godown

quiz.why: Parthenium (gajar ghas) is a weed, an unwanted plant in the field that competes with crops.

quiz.q: Insects damage crops by all EXCEPT
quiz.why: Insects damage crops by sucking sap, boring into stems and cutting leaves, but fixing nitrogen is done by certain bacteria, not insects.
Moisture and temperature are abiotic factors that can spoil stored grain. Insects, rats, fungi and mites are biotic.

quiz.q: Killing storage pests with chemical fumes is
quiz.why: Killing pests with chemical fumes in a closed space is fumigation. It is used for storing grain.

quiz.q: Deep ploughing in summer helps to
quiz.why: Deep ploughing in summer exposes weeds and pests to sun and kills them. It prepares the field.

lessons.title: Animal husbandry: cattle, poultry, fish and bees (extension)

story.title: The farm that does it all

scenes.text: Shanti's family farm earns from milk, eggs, a fish pond and bee boxes beside the mustard field.
Each needs different care — shelter, feed, disease control and good breeds.

steps.title: Cattle farming
steps.body: Two species: cows (*Bos indicus*) and buffaloes (*Bubalus bubalis*). **Milch animals** give milk; **draught animals** do farm labour. Exotic breeds (e.g. **Jersey, Brown Swiss**) are chosen for long lactation; local breeds (e.g. **Red Sindhi, Sahiwal**) for disease resistance — crossing them combines both. Needs: clean, well-ventilated, roofed shelter; regular cleaning and brushing; balanced feed of **roughage** (fibre) and **concentrates** (proteins, nutrients); vaccination against viral and bacterial diseases; control of external and internal parasites.

steps.title: Poultry
steps.body: Raising domestic fowl for eggs (**layers**) and meat (**broilers**). Improved varieties cross Indian breeds (e.g. **Aseel**) with exotic breeds (e.g. **Leghorn**) for number and quality of chicks, dwarfness for broiler parent stock, summer adaptation, low maintenance and smaller birds that use less feed. Broilers need protein- and vitamin-rich (A and K) feed; hygiene, proper temperature and vaccination prevent disease.

steps.title: Fish production
steps.body:
**Capture fishing** from natural resources; **culture fishery** (aquaculture) in ponds/tanks. Marine fish: pomphret, mackerel, tuna, sardines, Bombay duck; mariculture of mullets, bhetki, pearl spots, prawns, mussels, oysters (also for pearls). Inland: canals, ponds, reservoirs, rivers, estuaries.
**Composite fish culture**: 5–6 species in one pond, each using a different food zone so there is no competition — **catla** (surface), **rohu** (middle zone), **mrigal** and **common carp** (bottom), **grass carp** (weeds), with silver carp also used. A problem: some of these fish breed only during the monsoon, so pure seed supply is limited — now solved by hormonal stimulation of breeding in ponds.

steps.title: Bee-keeping (apiculture)
steps.body: Low-investment income from **honey** and **wax**. Varieties: *Apis cerana indica* (Indian bee), *A. dorsata* (rock bee), *A. florea* (little bee) and the Italian bee *A. mellifera*, preferred for high honey collection, gentleness (stings less), staying long in a hive and good breeding. **Pasturage** (flowers available) decides the quantity and the taste of honey.

steps.title: Solved: composite fish culture
steps.body: Why stock catla, rohu and mrigal together? They feed at the surface, middle and bottom respectively, so all of the pond's food is used and the fish don't compete — yield rises.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Saying broilers are reared for eggs (layers are).
- Saying composite culture uses one species.
- Saying honey taste is the same everywhere (depends on pasturage).

activity.prompt: Match the term

quiz.why: Draught animals, like bullocks, are used for farm labour such as ploughing and carrying loads.

quiz.q: A cattle feed rich in fibre is called
quiz.why: Roughage is cattle feed rich in fibre, like fodder. Concentrates are rich in proteins and other nutrients.

quiz.q: In composite fish culture, bottom feeders include
quiz.why: In composite fish culture, mrigal and common carp are bottom feeders. Catla feeds at the surface and rohu in the middle.

quiz.q: The Italian bee is preferred because it
options: collects more honey and stings less
quiz.why: The Italian bee is preferred because it collects more honey and stings less. It also breeds well.

options: flowers available for nectar and pollen
quiz.why: Pasturage means the flowers available for the bees to collect nectar and pollen. Honey quality depends on it.
Aseel is an Indian breed of poultry, known for its fighting qualities and meat. It is not a fish, cattle or bee.

questions.q: Rabi crops are sown in
questions.why: Rabi crops are sown in winter, around November, and harvested in spring. Kharif crops are sown in June-July.

questions.q: Which is a kharif crop?
questions.why: Paddy is a kharif crop, sown in the rainy season. Mustard, wheat and gram are rabi crops.

questions.q: Number of macronutrients obtained from soil
questions.why: Of the 13 nutrients from the soil, 6 are macronutrients (needed in large amounts) and 7 are micronutrients.

questions.q: Compost made with earthworms
questions.why: Compost made using earthworms is vermicompost. Humus is the dark organic part of the soil and urea is a fertiliser.

questions.q: Oilseeds provide mainly
questions.why: Oilseeds provide mainly fats, as in oils from groundnut and mustard. Pulses give proteins.

questions.q: Inter-cropping means crops grown
options: in a definite row pattern on the same field
questions.why: Inter-cropping means growing two or more crops in a definite pattern of rows on the same field. Mixed cropping has no pattern.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Mixed cropping reduces the risk of total crop failure. Reason (R): If one crop fails due to weather or pests, the other may survive.
options: Both true; R does not explain A
questions.why: Both are true and the reason explains the assertion. If one crop fails due to weather or pests, the other may survive, so total failure is less likely.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Excessive use of fertilisers improves soil fertility in the long run. Reason (R): Fertilisers add organic matter to the soil.
options: Both true; R does not explain A
questions.why: Both are false. Excess fertilisers do not add organic matter, and in the long run they can reduce soil fertility.

questions.q: Which pair are both micronutrients?
questions.why: Iron (Fe) and zinc (Zn) are micronutrients, needed in small amounts. K, Ca, Mg, S, N and P are macronutrients.

questions.q: A shorter maturity duration of a crop variety helps the farmer to
questions.why: A shorter maturity time lets the farmer grow more crops each year on the same field. It also saves water and labour.

questions.q: Biotic factors causing storage loss include
questions.why: Rodents and fungi are biotic factors that damage stored grain. Moisture, temperature and sunlight are abiotic.

questions.q: Case: A village's groundwater falls each year. Building small check-dams on local streams mainly helps by
options: increasing groundwater recharge and reducing run-off
questions.why: Check-dams hold back water and let it percolate, which recharges groundwater and reduces run-off. They don't add fertiliser or kill pests.

questions.q: Case: A farmer grows rice in kharif and wants to restore soil nitrogen before the next rice crop. The best rabi crop
questions.why: Gram, a legume, fixes nitrogen with the help of root bacteria, so it restores the soil nitrogen used by rice. Wheat and mustard take up nitrogen.

questions.q: Case: A fish farmer stocks only catla in a pond and finds bottom food unused. Adding which fish would best use it?
questions.why: Catla feeds at the surface, so the bottom food is unused. Mrigal and common carp are bottom feeders and would use it.

questions.q: A dairy farmer wants long lactation and disease resistance in one animal. Best approach
options: cross an exotic breed like Jersey with a local breed like Sahiwal
questions.why: Correct answer: cross an exotic breed like Jersey with a local breed like Sahiwal.

questions.q: Which statement about organic farming is correct?
options: It uses bio-agents such as blue-green algae and neem
questions.why: Organic farming uses natural methods, such as manure, crop rotation and bio-agents like blue-green algae and neem. It avoids chemical pesticides.

courses.title: Class 9 Science · Revision & Practice
courses.summary: One-page fact and formula sheets for the chemistry, biology and physics chapters of Class 9 Science, exam strategy, two mock papers and a full mixed test.
outcomes: Recall the key definitions, formulas and units of every chapter
Solve numericals on motion, force, gravitation, work–energy and sound quickly
Answer assertion–reason and case-based questions confidently
Self-assess with two mock papers and a final test

scenes.text: Kiran's chemistry test is tomorrow and she keeps mixing up colloids and suspensions.
One compact sheet with every definition side by side fixes the confusion.

steps.title: Matter and purity
steps.body:
- Particles: very small, spaces between, always moving (faster when hot), attract each other. Diffusion fastest in gases.
- K = °C + 273. Ice melts at 273 K; water boils at 373 K. Latent heat: fusion (solid → liquid), vaporisation (liquid → gas). Sublimation: camphor, naphthalene, NH₄Cl, iodine; dry ice = solid CO₂.
- Evaporation ↑ with surface area, temperature, wind; ↓ with humidity; causes cooling.
- Solution (< 1 nm, no Tyndall), colloid (1–1000 nm, Tyndall, centrifuge), suspension (visible, settles, filterable).
- Mass % = solute/solution × 100. Compounds: fixed ratio, new properties; mixtures: variable, keep properties.

steps.title: Atoms and the atom
steps.body:
- Conservation of mass (Lavoisier); constant proportions (Proust; H : O = 1 : 8 in water). Dalton's atomic theory.
- 1 u = 1/12 mass of C-12. Molecular mass = sum of atomic masses (H₂O 18, CO₂ 44, H₂SO₄ 98, NaCl 58.5).
- Criss-cross valencies: Al₂O₃, Ca(OH)₂, (NH₄)₂SO₄.
- e⁻ (Thomson), canal rays/p⁺ (Goldstein), n (Chadwick 1932). Rutherford: nucleus, mostly empty space. Bohr: fixed orbits, no radiation.
- Shell capacity 2n²; outermost ≤ 8. Valency = valence e⁻ or 8 − valence e⁻.
- A = p + n; isotopes same Z (U-235 fuel, Co-60 cancer, I-131 goitre); isobars same A (⁴⁰Ca, ⁴⁰Ar).

steps.title: Quick drill
steps.body: 1) 27 °C = 300 K. 2) 20 g salt in 180 g water → 10%. 3) Formula unit mass of CaCl₂ = 111 u. 4) S (16): 2, 8, 6, valency 2. 5) Neutrons in ³⁵Cl = 18.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Adding instead of subtracting 273 (or vice versa).
- Dividing by solvent mass in concentration.
- Calling milk a solution.

cards.back: scattering of light by colloid/suspension particles
heat to melt 1 kg at its melting point
1/12 of the mass of a C-12 atom
same atomic number, different mass number
same mass number, different atomic numbers

quiz.why: Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide. It sublimes straight to gas, leaving no liquid.
Colloid particles have a size between 1 and 1000 nm. They are larger than particles of a true solution, but smaller than those of a suspension.
Chlorine (2, 8, 7) needs 1 more electron to complete its octet, so its valency is 1.

U-235 is a fissile isotope: its nucleus splits when it absorbs a neutron, releasing energy and more neutrons for a chain reaction. Co-60, I-131 and C-14 are used in medicine, therapy or dating, not as reactor fuel.

scenes.text: Biology answers need exact words — 'selectively permeable', 'suicide bags', 'apical meristem'.
This sheet lists the words examiners look for.

steps.title: Cell
steps.body:
- Hooke 1665 (cork); Leeuwenhoek 1674; Brown 1831 (nucleus); Purkinje 1839 (protoplasm); Schleiden & Schwann (cell theory); Virchow 1855 (cells from cells).
- Plasma membrane: selectively permeable (lipids + proteins). Diffusion; osmosis (water across a membrane); hypotonic → swells, isotonic → no change, hypertonic → shrinks. Plasmolysis in plant cells.
- Cell wall: cellulose. Prokaryote: nucleoid, no membrane-bound organelles.
- ER (RER proteins, SER lipids/detox), Golgi (package/dispatch), lysosome (suicide bag), mitochondria (ATP, own DNA), plastids (chloroplast/leucoplast, own DNA), vacuole.
- Mitosis: 2 identical cells; meiosis: 4 cells, half chromosomes (gametes).

steps.title: Tissues
steps.body:
- Meristem: apical (length), lateral/cambium (girth), intercalary (base of leaves/internodes); no vacuoles.
- Parenchyma (store; chlorenchyma, aerenchyma), collenchyma (flexibility), sclerenchyma (dead, lignin). Epidermis (cutin, stomata), cork (suberin).
- Xylem: tracheids, vessels, parenchyma, fibres — water up. Phloem: sieve tubes, companion cells, parenchyma, fibres (only dead part) — food both ways.
- Epithelium: squamous, stratified (skin), columnar (intestine; ciliated in airways), cuboidal (kidney tubules), glandular. Connective: blood, bone, ligament (bone–bone), tendon (muscle–bone), cartilage, areolar, adipose. Muscles: striated (voluntary, multinucleate), smooth (involuntary, spindle), cardiac (branched). Neuron: dendrites, cell body, axon.

steps.title: Food resources
steps.body:
- Kharif (June–Oct): paddy, soybean, maize, cotton, pulses (arhar, moong, urad). Rabi (Nov–Apr): wheat, gram, peas, mustard, linseed.
- 16 nutrients: C, H, O from air/water; macro N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S; micro Fe, Mn, B, Zn, Cu, Mo, Cl.
- Manure (compost, vermicompost, green manure) vs fertiliser (NPK). Mixed cropping, inter-cropping, crop rotation. Storage: clean, dry, fumigate.

steps.title: Quick drill
steps.body: 1) Organelle with digestive enzymes → lysosome. 2) RBC in pure water → swells/bursts. 3) Coconut husk → sclerenchyma. 4) Ligament joins → bone to bone. 5) Wheat → rabi.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Ligament vs tendon.
- Cutin (epidermis) vs suberin (cork).
- Kharif vs rabi months.

activity.prompt: Match

quiz.why: Schleiden (botanist) and Schwann (zoologist) proposed that all living things are made of cells. Virchow later added that new cells arise from existing cells; Hooke only observed and named cells.

In a hypertonic solution the outside has more solute, so water leaves the cell by osmosis through the membrane. Losing water makes the cell shrink; swelling or bursting happens in a hypotonic solution.

quiz.q: The only dead component of phloem
quiz.why: Sieve tubes, companion cells and phloem parenchyma are living cells. Phloem fibres are sclerenchyma with thick lignified walls and no living contents, so they are the dead component.
Voluntary muscles, such as those of the arms and legs, show light and dark bands under a microscope, so they are called striated. Smooth muscles are involuntary; cardiac muscle is involuntary too.
Micronutrients are needed by plants in very small amounts; zinc is one. Potassium, sulphur and calcium are needed in large amounts, so they are macronutrients.

scenes.text: Arjun knows the theory but freezes on numericals.
He writes the formula, lists given values with units, substitutes and checks units — every time.

steps.title: Motion and force
steps.body:
- Speed = distance/time; 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s; average velocity (uniform a) = (u + v)/2.
- a = (v − u)/t. Graphs: slope of s–t = speed; slope of v–t = a; area under v–t = displacement.
- v = u + at; s = ut + ½at²; v² − u² = 2as. Circular: v = 2πr/t.
- p = mv; F = ma = Δp/t; impulse F·t = Δp; action = −reaction; m₁u₁ + m₂u₂ = m₁v₁ + m₂v₂.

steps.title: Gravitation, work and energy
steps.body:
- F = Gm₁m₂/d², G = 6.673 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²; g = GM/R² ≈ 9.8 m/s²; W = mg; Moon ≈ 1/6.
- P = F/A (Pa); upthrust = weight of fluid displaced; RD = density/1000 kg m⁻³.
- W = Fs (J); KE = ½mv²; PE = mgh; PE + KE constant in free fall; P = W/t (W); 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.

steps.title: Sound
steps.body:
- v = λν; T = 1/ν; audible 20 Hz–20 kHz; pitch ↔ frequency, loudness ↔ amplitude.
- Echo: d = vt/2, minimum distance ≈ 17.2 m (v = 344 m/s, 0.1 s). SONAR depth = vt/2. Speed: solids > liquids > gases.

steps.title: Quick drill
steps.body: 1) 90 km/h = 25 m/s. 2) From rest, a = 3 m/s² for 4 s ⇒ v = 12 m/s, s = 24 m. 3) 2 kg, F = 10 N ⇒ a = 5 m/s². 4) KE of 4 kg at 3 m/s = 18 J. 5) Echo 1.5 s, v = 340 ⇒ 255 m.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Not converting km/h, g, cm², minutes.
- Forgetting ½ in KE and s = ut + ½at², or the halving in echo/SONAR.
- Writing m/s for acceleration.

quiz.q: Area under a velocity–time graph gives
quiz.why: Velocity = displacement/time, so the area under a velocity–time graph (velocity × time) equals displacement. The slope of that graph gives acceleration, not the area.

quiz.q: A 3 kg mass accelerates at 4 m/s². Force
quiz.why: Force = mass × acceleration = 3 kg × 4 m/s² = 12 N. The other values come from dividing or adding the numbers instead of multiplying.
Weight = mass × g = 50 × 9.8 = 490 N. Weight is a force measured in newtons; 50 kg is the mass, which stays the same everywhere.
Potential energy = mgh = 5 × 10 × 4 = 200 J. Multiply mass, g and height; 40 J or 20 J come from leaving out a factor.

quiz.q: λ for 680 Hz in air at 340 m/s
quiz.why: Wavelength = speed ÷ frequency = 340 ÷ 680 = 0.5 m. A higher frequency at the same speed gives a shorter wavelength.

scenes.text: Set a 25-minute timer. No notes.
Mark yourself, then revise the chapter for every miss.

steps.title: How to use
steps.body: 8 mixed questions across chemistry, biology and physics. Write formula → values → substitution → answer with unit for numericals.

steps.title: Strategy
steps.body:
- Attempt sure questions first.
- For assertion–reason: judge A, then R, then whether R explains A.
- For case-based questions: underline the data in the case before reading the options.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Missing units.
- Reading 'NOT' or 'EXCEPT' too quickly.

activity.prompt: Before you start
items: Plan: easy first, check units at the end

options: water spread on a plate on a windy sunny day
quiz.why: Evaporation is fastest with a large surface area, high temperature, wind and low humidity. Water spread on a plate on a windy, sunny day has all of these; the other cases limit surface, air movement or dryness.

quiz.q: A solution has 15 g solute in 135 g water. Mass %
quiz.why: Mass % = solute ÷ solution × 100. The solution is 15 + 135 = 150 g, so 15/150 × 100 = 10%. The common slip, 15/135, ignores the solute's own mass.
Aluminium is Al³⁺ and sulphate is SO₄²⁻. Criss-cross the charges: 2 Al³⁺ (+6) balance 3 SO₄²⁻ (−6), giving Al₂(SO₄)₃.
Oxygen has Z = 8, so 8 electrons in the atom. O²⁻ has gained 2 electrons, so 8 + 2 = 10 electrons, the same as neon.
The Golgi apparatus receives substances made in the cell, packs them into vesicles and sends them to where they are needed. Lysosomes digest waste, ribosomes make proteins and the nucleus holds DNA.

quiz.q: A car from 0 to 30 m/s in 10 s: distance
quiz.why: Starting from rest, s = ½ × v × t = ½ × 30 × 10 = 150 m using the average speed 15 m/s. Using 30 × 10 = 300 m wrongly assumes the car moved at top speed throughout.

quiz.q: A gun of 5 kg fires a 20 g bullet at 500 m/s. Recoil speed
quiz.why: Momentum is conserved. Bullet momentum = 0.02 × 500 = 10 kg m/s, so the gun recoils with 10 ÷ 5 = 2 m/s in the opposite direction.

quiz.q: SONAR echo after 2.4 s, v = 1500 m/s. Depth
quiz.why: The sound travels to the sea bed and back, so depth = v × t ÷ 2 = 1500 × 2.4 ÷ 2 = 1800 m. 3600 m forgets to halve for the round trip.

scenes.text: A week later, try the second paper.
Compare your score with Mock Paper 1 and update your error log.

steps.title: How to use
steps.body: Another 8 mixed questions, slightly harder. 25 minutes.

steps.title: Error log
steps.body: For each mistake write: chapter, what went wrong (concept / calculation / reading), and the fix. Review the log before the final test.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Revising only favourite chapters.
- Not re-attempting wrong questions.

activity.prompt: After the paper
items: Ready for the final mixed test

quiz.q: Steam at 100 °C burns more than water at 100 °C because
options: it carries extra latent heat of vaporisation
quiz.why: Steam at 100 °C holds extra latent heat of vaporisation (about 2260 J per gram) that it releases when it condenses on skin. Water at the same temperature lacks this extra heat, so steam burns more.

quiz.q: A mixture of ethanol (351 K) and water (373 K) is separated by
quiz.why: The boiling points differ by 22 K, which is small, so simple distillation cannot separate them cleanly. Fractional distillation with a fractionating column is used for miscible liquids with close boiling points.

quiz.q: Average atomic mass of an element with ¹⁰X 20% and ¹¹X 80%
quiz.why: Average mass = (10 × 20 + 11 × 80)/100 = (200 + 880)/100 = 10.8 u. The result is closer to 11 because the heavier isotope is more abundant.

quiz.q: Cells of a tissue are long, dead and lignified. The tissue is
quiz.why: Sclerenchyma cells are long, dead and have lignified thick walls, giving strength. Parenchyma and collenchyma are living tissues, and meristem is made of dividing cells.

quiz.q: If the distance between two masses is halved, the gravitational force
quiz.why: Gravitational force is proportional to 1/d². Halving d gives 1/(½)² = 4, so the force becomes 4 times larger. It does not simply double.

quiz.q: A 60 kg man climbs 10 m in 20 s (g = 10). Power
quiz.why: Work = mgh = 60 × 10 × 10 = 6000 J. Power = work ÷ time = 6000 ÷ 20 = 300 W. 6000 W forgets to divide by time.

quiz.q: Velocity 10 m/s to 30 m/s in 4 s; distance covered
quiz.why: Average velocity = (10 + 30)/2 = 20 m/s, so distance = 20 × 4 = 80 m. Using only the final speed would overestimate the distance.

quiz.q: Composite fish culture works because the species
options: feed in different zones of the pond
quiz.why: In composite fish culture, species such as catla, rohu and mrigal feed at different levels of the pond (surface, middle, bottom). They do not compete much, so the pond gives more fish.

questions.q: Which is a chemical change?
questions.why: Burning wood forms new substances such as ash, carbon dioxide and water vapour, and it cannot be reversed. Melting, evaporating and dissolving only change the state or mixing, so they are physical changes.

questions.q: Symbol of sodium
questions.why: The symbol of sodium comes from its Latin name natrium, so it is Na. S stands for sulphur and N for nitrogen.

questions.q: Plant cell wall is made of
questions.why: The plant cell wall is made of cellulose, a tough carbohydrate. Chitin forms fungal walls and insect shells; lipids and proteins are not the main wall material.

questions.q: SI unit of power
questions.why: Power is the rate of doing work, and its SI unit is the watt (1 J/s). Newton is for force, pascal for pressure and joule for energy.

questions.q: Convert 300 K to °C
questions.why: °C = K − 273, so 300 − 273 = 27 °C. Adding 273 would give 573, which is wrong for this direction.

questions.q: Valency of aluminium
questions.why: Aluminium has 3 valence electrons (2, 8, 3), and it loses them to form Al³⁺, so its valency is 3.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Mitochondria can make some of their own proteins. Reason (R): They have their own DNA and ribosomes.
options: Both true; R does not explain A
questions.why: Both statements are true: mitochondria hold their own DNA and ribosomes, so they can make some of their own proteins. The reason directly explains the assertion.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Sound travels faster in steel than in air. Reason (R): Sound needs a medium to travel.
options: Both true; R does not explain A
questions.why: Both statements are true. Sound is faster in steel because steel is much stiffer and its particles transmit vibrations faster. Needing a medium is true, but it does not explain why steel is faster than air.

questions.q: Molecular mass of C₂H₅OH
questions.why: C₂H₅OH: 2 × 12 + 5 × 1 + 16 + 1 = 24 + 5 + 16 + 1 = 46 u. Add the mass of every atom in the formula, including the hydrogen in OH.

questions.q: Tissue connecting muscle to bone
questions.why: A tendon joins muscle to bone. A ligament joins bone to bone, and cartilage is a smooth cushioning tissue at joints.

questions.q: A body of mass 2 kg moves at 10 m/s. Its momentum and KE
questions.why: Momentum = mv = 2 × 10 = 20 kg m/s. KE = ½mv² = ½ × 2 × 100 = 100 J. Other options mix up the formulas or forget the square.

questions.q: Case: In Rutherford's experiment, if 1 in 12 000 α-particles bounced back, this mainly shows
options: the nucleus is tiny, dense and positive
questions.why: Most α-particles passed straight through, but very few bounced back. This showed that the positive charge and mass are packed into a tiny, dense nucleus. It did not show that atoms are solid.

questions.q: Case: A 10 kg block on a 0.5 m² base is stacked with an identical block (g = 10). Pressure on the floor
questions.why: The floor carries both blocks: weight = 20 kg × 10 = 200 N. Pressure = force ÷ area = 200 ÷ 0.5 = 400 Pa. Using only one block would give 200 Pa.

questions.q: A ball is thrown up at 25 m/s (g = 10). Time to reach maximum height and the height
questions.why: At the top v = 0, so t = u/g = 25/10 = 2.5 s. Height = u²/2g = 625/20 = 31.25 m. Time up is u/g, not 2u/g (that is the full flight).

questions.q: A sea-bed is 3000 m deep; SONAR speed 1500 m/s. Echo time
questions.why: The echo covers the depth twice, so t = 2d/v = 2 × 3000 ÷ 1500 = 4 s. Using d/v = 2 s forgets the return trip.

questions.q: An element has configuration 2, 8, 8, 2. Its atomic number, valency and name
questions.why: The configuration 2, 8, 8, 2 has 2 + 8 + 8 + 2 = 20 electrons, so the atomic number is 20 (calcium). It has 2 outer electrons, so its valency is 2.

questions.q: A 1000 kg car at 72 km/h stops in 50 m. Average braking force
questions.why: 72 km/h = 20 m/s. From v² = u² + 2as, 0 = 400 + 2a(50), so a = −4 m/s². Force = ma = 1000 × 4 = 4000 N.

questions.q: A piece of iron of volume 100 cm³ (density 7.9 g/cm³) is fully immersed in water. Upthrust (g = 10)
questions.why: Upthrust equals the weight of water displaced. 100 cm³ of water has mass 100 g = 0.1 kg, so upthrust = 0.1 × 10 = 1 N. The density of iron is not needed.

questions.q: A lamp of 100 W and a heater of 1.5 kW each run 4 hours. Total energy
questions.why: Energy = power × time. Lamp: 0.1 kW × 4 h = 0.4 kWh. Heater: 1.5 kW × 4 h = 6 kWh. Total = 0.4 + 6 = 6.4 kWh; convert 100 W to 0.1 kW first.
